text: A claim about what a change does was computed from a reimplementation of one predicate rather than from the command that decides. The 0.10.0 release body said eight of sixty-six baseline pairs move 'unchanged' to 'unknown'; the eight share a build but differ in scope, and 'diff' refuses them at SESSION_BASELINE_NOT_COMPARABLE before MethodChange is reached, so no comparison in the ledger moves at all. Build equality was the predicate I wrote; scope refusal is the predicate the act applies first. The release skill already requires the opposite — 'Diff the gate over a corpus before and after' means run the gate, twice — so this is a rule broken rather than a rule missing, and the discipline that catches it is running the thing rather than reading harder. Found by running the published binary on the real ledger at step 4, after the tag was pushed. A sibling repository reports the same class from two further origins, both wrong-predicate rather than wrong-prose: a landing precondition reading 'git status --porcelain' where its own code documents 'target_is_pristine' as the oracle, and an exit condition requiring the landing it exists to release.
source: 0.10.0 release body, caught at step 4 by the published binary; aix-platform reports two further origins, 2026-09-06
